outcome: The general conjecture remains open, but the minimum-out-degree threshold for which it is proved was pushed from 6 (Kaneko-Locke, 2001) to 7 by Sadhukhan, Sandeep and Sen (arXiv:2606.30588, June 2026), a genuine restriction/case of the stated problem; separately Huang and Peng (arXiv:2412.20234, Dec 2024) improved the best known universal constant factor to 0.715538, and a self-published preprint by Charles N. Glover (arXiv:2501.00614) claims a full proof but has not been accepted by the field, which continues to describe the conjecture as open as of mid-2026.

disputes.summary: Charles N. Glover's arXiv:2501.00614 claims a full constructive proof of the general conjecture via a self-invented 'Graph Level Order' (GLOVER) framework, first posted 31 Dec 2024 and revised through at least v14 (May 2026). It is self-published (personal site glovermethod.com, GitHub repo, 'AlphaXiv' posting), shows no sign of journal acceptance or expert digestion, and a later 2026 paper on the same conjecture (arXiv:2607.18047) explicitly states the general conjecture 'remains open for general oriented graphs' without flagging Glover's claim as a resolution. This is treated here as an unaccepted claim, not a resolution.

summary: Three lines of genuine, in-scope progress on the second neighborhood problem occurred in the window. (1) Huang and Peng (arXiv:2412.20234, submitted 28 Dec 2024) proved every oriented graph has a vertex u with |N++(u)| ≥ 0.715538|N+(u)|, the first improvement to the universal constant bound in over two decades (previous best ~0.6839, Chen-Shen-Yuster). This is `progress`: the general conjecture (constant 1) is still open, but the approximation constant moved, which is the quantity the bullet is asking about. (2) Sadhukhan, Sandeep and Sen (arXiv:2606.30588, submitted 29 Jun 2026) proved the full conjecture (constant exactly 1) for oriented graphs with minimum out-degree equal to 7, extending the Kaneko-Locke (2001) result for out-degree ≤6 — a genuine restriction (case) of the stated problem, hence `partial` with direction `confirmed`. Their proof is 'partially computer-assisted' via OR-Tools CP-SAT infeasibility checks on finite obstruction models after local reductions — this is a constraint-satisfaction solver, not a machine-learning/AI system, so `ai_role` is `none` for this event. (3) Charles N. Glover's arXiv:2501.00614 (first posted 31 Dec 2024, now at v14, May 2026) claims a full proof of the general conjecture via a self-devised 'GLOVER' minimum-counterexample framework. This preprint shows the hallmarks of an unaccepted claim: extreme revision churn (14 versions over 17 months), self-publication on a personal site and GitHub rather than through a venue with expert referees, and — most tellingly — a subsequent 2026 arXiv paper on the same topic (2607.18047, 'Towards a strengthening of the second neighborhood conjecture') that still describes the general conjecture as open, with no acknowledgment of Glover's claim as resolving it. No expert digestion (Tao's blog, Quanta, a survey, or a published refutation) of Glover's claim was found either way. Since the overall record for this bullet should reflect the best-supported status across the found events, and the highest-confidence, expert-uncontested event is the out-degree-7 case proof, the record is classified `partial` (confirmed direction) rather than `claimed`/`resolved` on the strength of Glover's unaccepted claim alone; Glover's claim itself is recorded as a dispute rather than driving the status. No AI system (LLM or otherwise) was found credited by authors for producing any of the mathematics in any of these three results; the only computational tool disclosed is a classical constraint solver (OR-Tools CP-SAT), which the coding rules exclude from AI credit.
competing_reading: One could argue the record should be `claimed` if Glover's arXiv:2501.00614 is read as the decisive event, since it purports to fully resolve the general conjecture (a stronger claim than the out-degree-7 case). Against this: the claim has had 17+ months and 14 revisions without visible expert acceptance, and a 2026 paper in the same subfield still calls the conjecture open, which is strong (if indirect) evidence the community has not accepted it. I weighted the accepted, narrower result (out-degree 7) as the status-defining event and demoted Glover's claim to a dispute; a stricter reading of `claimed` ("a preprint... that experts have not yet digested") could support listing Glover's paper as the primary `event` instead, with status `claimed`, while still keeping the out-degree-7 result as a secondary `partial` fact in the summary.
what_would_settle_it: An expert digestion (a survey, a rebuttal, MathOverflow/blog discussion, or a journal referee report) explicitly addressing whether Glover's GLOVER proof is correct, or its formal withdrawal/retraction, would resolve whether this bullet should be `resolved`/`claimed` on that basis or continue to rest on the accepted partial results.
